description: 2 tactical challenges for Black in the Rousseau Gambit. Strike with 3...f5!? and seize the initiative.

drills.briefExplanation: 3...f5 4.exf5 e4 5.Nd4 Nf6 — Black sacrifices for open lines and a kingside attack.
drills.description: Black to play. White plays the Italian 3.Bc4 — counter with the Rousseau 3...f5!.
drills.explanation: The Rousseau Gambit: Black meets the Italian Game with a King's Gambit reversed. After 4.exf5 e4 the f3 knight must move, and 5.Nd4 Nf6 gives Black the classic gambit setup — open f-file, mobile center, and attacking chances against White's king. White's extra pawn is shaky; Black's initiative is real.
drills.name: The Rousseau Strike

drills.briefExplanation: 5...Nf6 6.Nxc6 bxc6 7.Nc3 d5 — give back the piece for a rolling pawn center.
drills.description: Black to play. White retreated 5.Nd4 — develop and prepare the central break.
drills.explanation: After 5...Nf6 White's knight is awkward on d4. 6.Nxc6 bxc6 opens the b-file and, more importantly, prepares 7...d5! — Black's pawn center starts rolling. White's f5 pawn will fall, the e4 pawn cramps White's game, and Black's bishops will rake the long diagonals. Gambit compensation, textbook-style.
drills.name: The Pawn Roller
